To solve this they experimented with different marketing strategies and offered discounts and incentives to dealers. Despite these efforts, the Maverick never became a huge success. To deal with the huge inventory they had, Ford decided to find a place to store the unsold cars until they could weather the storm. Parking the unsold Mavericks above ground would have damaged the new cars and cause other long-term problems. Ford decided to store the unsold Mavericks in the Subtropolis caves located in Kansas City, Missouri. The caves proved to be the ideal climate-controlled environment for several months until the market improved. At its peak, Ford stored as many as 14,000 Mavericks in the caves. The cars were organized in neat rows, and employees were responsible to move them occasionally to prevent any damage from them sitting in one place for too long. To answer your question, what are some crisis management techniques? By limiting the supply, Ford was able to create a sense of scarcity around the Maverick, which helped protect their unsold cars and maintain its value. #BeBusinessSmart
